entities.description: Electrical device that transfers electrical energy between circuits through electromagnetic induction.
Electric current which periodically reverses direction, creating a changing magnetic field.
Electric current flowing in one constant direction, producing a constant unchanging magnetic field.
Field produced by electric currents; must change in intensity/direction to induce electromotive force.
Mathematical waveform describing the periodic oscillation of alternating current.
Induced electrical action produced by a changing magnetic field disturbing free electrons in a conductor.
Loops of conductive wire wrapped to concentrate magnetic flux.
High-permeability ferromagnetic loop placed between coils to guide magnetic flux.
Loops of electrical current induced within conductors by a changing magnetic field, causing resistive heat losses.
Thin insulated sheets of iron stacked to form the core and suppress circulating eddy currents.
Transformer that increases output secondary voltage while reducing output current via more secondary coil turns.
Transformer that decreases output secondary voltage while increasing output current via fewer secondary coil turns.
Electric potential difference between points in the circuit.
Flow of electric charge carriers (electrons) through a conductor.
Arrangement using three alternating currents of the same frequency with a phase difference, used in commercial distribution.
Wiring configuration with primary coils in delta (triangle) and secondary coils in wye/star with a grounded neutral line.
